narrative.bottom_line: The regime model reads neutral at a composite of 0.08, and the market signals behind it justify the label: equities sit above their 200-day average and volatility is contained. The hard data is thinner than that, with hiring stalled and inflation reaccelerating on a commodity shock. Equities are priced for continuity while the inputs beneath them diverge.
paragraphs: Output is strong, hiring has stopped, and households feel the second more than the first. Real GDP grew at a 3.4% annual rate last quarter, so the strain sits in hiring, not output. Payrolls added only 29,000 in September while claims near 194,000 stay historically low, so firms freeze hiring rather than cut. Consumer sentiment of 48.1 is the weakest in seven decades, and a 3.8% savings rate leaves no cushion.

A commodity shock has pushed inflation back up while long yields sit near twenty-year highs. Headline PCE at 3.65% and core at 3.12% both sit above target, with services and energy still pushing. The IMF commodity index is up 55% over a year and Brent sits at $123, feeding goods and transport costs. The 10-year Treasury yield at 4.98% sits in the 99th percentile of 20 years, repricing every long-duration asset.

Credit conditions remain easy overall at -0.49 on the Chicago Fed index, with stress confined to the bottom tier. Investment-grade spreads at 89bp widened only 5bp over the month, pricing a slowdown rather than a default cycle. CCC spreads jumped from 11.79% to 13.25% in a month, so the weakest borrowers are already being cut off. The broad dollar index at 121.32, the 89th percentile of 20 years, tightens funding abroad and trims translated earnings.
watch: Initial claims above 250,000 would turn a hiring freeze into layoffs and end the consumption story.
Five-year forward inflation above 2.6% would show the commodity shock leaking into expectations and locking the Fed.
High-yield spreads past 450bp would mark funding stress spreading beyond the weakest tier into ordinary balance sheets.
narrative.international: Inflation is the shared constraint abroad: euro-area HICP at 3.75% holds the ECB at a restrictive stance, while the yen near 157 per dollar keeps Japanese import costs and JGB yields climbing. China diverges sharply, its equities down 22% over the year as the rest of emerging markets advanced. Dollar strength against that backdrop caps US overseas earnings.

sectors.influence: The 10-year real yield of 2.63% sits atop its 20-year range, discounting long-dated software earnings hardest. Stalled hiring trims corporate IT budgets. The AI capex cycle still funds orders, and that structural pull narrowly wins.
sectors.headline: Real yields bill the future

sectors.influence: The 10-year to 2-year spread of 38bp leaves little margin to earn on the loan book. CCC spreads blowing out raises provisioning risk ahead of revenue. Curve normalisation, the sector's main structural hope, has not yet arrived.
sectors.headline: A thin curve, fat risks

sectors.influence: Defensive money is moving: healthcare has outrun the market by 16% over three months as growth signals soften. High long rates matter little to these cash flows. Aging-demographic volume growth reinforces the rotation, and it dominates now.
sectors.headline: Defence pays its way

sectors.influence: Retail sales up 6.3% year on year flatter a consumer whose credit is growing only 2.7%. High mortgage costs still block big-ticket and housing-adjacent demand. The structural rate-cut trigger for autos and durables has not fired.
sectors.headline: Spending on a thin cushion

sectors.influence: Global food prices up 10.5% over the year squeeze packaged-goods margins before pricing catches up. Weak household confidence pushes capital toward predictable earnings. Proven pricing power in essentials offsets the cost side, leaving the sector a mild winner.
sectors.headline: Staples weather the grocery bill

sectors.influence: The sector trades 11% below its 200-day average, the market's weakest tape, as ad budgets track a shaky consumer. Elevated real yields compress its growth multiple. Retail-media mix shift helps, but cyclical ad risk dominates now.
sectors.headline: Ad dollars go missing

sectors.influence: Industrial relative strength of -8% is the weakest input in the regime model. Production growth of 2.2% year on year sits below its long-run median. Reshoring and defence capex cushion the cycle but have not reversed it.
sectors.headline: Factories lose the lead

sectors.influence: WTI crude at $103 a barrel, the 92nd percentile of 20 years, converts straight into cash flow. The sector trades 20% above its 200-day average, the market's clear leader. Capital discipline turns that price into dividends rather than drilling.
sectors.headline: Crude does the heavy lifting

sectors.influence: Copper at a record $14,473 a tonne and steel PPI up 66% year on year lift producer revenue. A dollar near 20-year highs works the other way. Thin supply after a decade of underinvestment tips the balance positive.
sectors.headline: Metals up, dollar in the way

sectors.influence: The 30-year Treasury at 5.32% gives income investors a competing yield and raises the cost of rate-base capital. Retail electricity prices at a 35-year high support revenue. AI-driven load growth is the structural offset, and it roughly balances.
sectors.headline: Load growth meets bond yields

sectors.influence: The 30-year mortgage at 7.24%, near a 20-year high, keeps cap rates elevated and refinancing expensive. Housing starts of 1.22 million sit in the 25th percentile of 68 years. Data-centre REIT demand offsets part of it, not enough.
sectors.headline: Cap rates refuse to fall
